lots.confidence_reason: Marks read in the photos (Hibernia, crowned harp, Victoria duty head, V in pointed shield) but maker mark is worn and unread and the date letter cycle was not checked against a table. No same-item SOLD evidence; only loose Gowans comparables.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's combined entry ('$110 and $65 hammers (two lots)', aud_price 65): the price label did not match the lots cited (375054 actually sold $33 and 424085 sold $130 per the API), it merged two sales into an invented midpoint, and both were salt cellars or dishes, not spoons. Re-filed 425811 Sargisons pair from close to category guide.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 enlarged: from top, a worn maker mark (two letters, unread), oval Victoria duty head, Hibernia, crowned harp, then date letter V in a pointed-base shield, consistent with Dublin c.1840. Both spoons carry the same mark set (photo 2). Front shows engraved script monogram LH on both terminals. Bowls show light scratches and small dings; a small nick on the terminal edge in photo 3. No obvious splits or repairs.
lots.condition: Used, light wear and scratching, small nicks; monogrammed; marks clear except the maker mark.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the maker's mark and that both spoons are matching Dublin pieces with no repairs? (Two other Dublin spoon pairs, catalogue ids 443514 and 443593, are in the same sale, so buyers' money will be split.)
